sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Arihant Academy is a regional classroom and hybrid coaching network expanding through new centres and acquisitions. The strength is substantial revenue growth with positive cumulative cash generation; the decisive risk is whether new cohorts and contractual revenue earn cash returns after faculty, rent, setup costs and acquisition payments. At the dated October 7 price of ₹230, the central financed scenario earns about 7.9% annually against a 15% analytical hurdle. Episodic trading makes execution a separate constraint. This is a growth-expansion research thesis, not an evidence-backed compounder or a purchase recommendation. [S1, S8, S10, M1]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Research cutoff: October 20, 2026, UTC; latest completed exchange session October 19, with the last observed Arihant trade on October 7. NSE SME symbol ARIHANTACA, ISIN INE0NCC01015, 12,110,400 shares after the October 5 bonus allotment, board lot 800. Dated market value is ₹278.5392 crore. AS-based FY25–26 accounts equity-account ZEAL; the June 2026 quarter consolidates it from April 1. Five-year horizon, 15% nominal pre-investor-tax hurdle and illustrative ₹5 lakh liquidity reference apply. All gates are conditional, not automatic failures: financial display reconciliations, acquisition obligations and thin execution remain explicit. Overall material evidence confidence is Medium. [S1, S4, S5, S7, S8, M1]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors are GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 6, CASH 6, BAL 6, EXEC 6 and EARN 6; IAS factors are R 2, D 4, P 3 and L 1. The audit retains exact weights and unrounded arithmetic, with no hidden haircut or missing-factor renormalization. BAL is reduced from the earlier 7 because the linked no-new-credit bear reveals a meaningful funding need. No severe governance, present funding-failure or accounting-reliability override is established. IAS is conditional on the dated quote, not automatically NS because probabilities are unassigned. [E1–E8]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: Students and families buy school-board, science, commerce and competitive-exam preparation, including JEE, NEET, MHT-CET, CA and CS. Tuition receipts can precede teaching, creating fee-advance liabilities; recognition follows service delivery. Contractual arrangements are recognized against milestones and account for a distinct collection risk. Faculty/professional charges and leased premises are major operating costs, so this is not a software-like near-zero marginal-cost model. The October 17 announcement describes more than 40 branches in 10 cities across three states and more than 15,000 students; these are issuer-reported scale measures, not audited same-centre cohorts. [S1 notes 17, 21 and revenue policy; S10]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Forty operating centres and more than 15,000 current-year students are issuer-reported operating scale, distinct from cumulative 190,000+ students. Local teaching reputation and multi-curriculum offerings can help referrals; they do not prove durable pricing power or low faculty churn. FY26 acquisitions and centre expansion add access, but comparable-centre enrolment, retention and realized fee growth were not disclosed in reviewed tables. A premium recurring-software multiple is inappropriate for labour-intensive classroom delivery. [S1 p.5] Relevant comparisons are Career Launcher for national test-prep reach, Veranda/J.K. Shah for commerce competition, and NIIT Learning Systems only as a contrasting enterprise-learning model. None supplies an unadjusted valuation multiple for Arihant. [P1–P3]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Verified revenue is ₹14.0803/15.2067/23.1181/30.3235/40.5571/63.4314 crore in FY21–26. Five-year growth begins in the pandemic period; the preselected three-year FY23–26 window is approximately 40.0%, with acquisitions and no verified organic decomposition. The shorter FY24–26 CAGR is 44.64%, not the only window displayed. FY26 service revenue is ₹55.9484 crore and other operating revenue ₹7.4830 crore, versus ₹40.5571 crore entirely classified as services in FY25. June-quarter parent sales increased 14.97% to ₹19.8320 crore and parent PAT 4.71% to ₹2.0522 crore. Group sales ₹22.0042 crore include newly consolidated ZEAL and are not a like-for-like organic growth rate. [S1, S8, S12–S14]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The multi-year capital proxy includes goodwill and CWIP rather than excluding unfinished or acquired capital. FY25–26 ΔNOPAT/ΔIC is about 46.6%; extending to FY23–26 and normalizing the opening exceptional depreciation lowers the proxy to roughly 28%, still above the assumed 12–16% capital-cost range. Fee advances and acquisitions distort the denominator, so CAP remains mixed at 6 rather than exceptional. Base growth of 15% requires an illustrative 12% enrollment increase plus 2.68% fee/mix increase, alongside actual reinvestment and working-capital changes. New Ahmedabad branches and ZEAL control broaden access, but neither proves mature-centre profitability. The model funds the earnout and new setup costs explicitly. [S1, S2, S5, S8, S10, S12, S13]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Director remuneration was ₹0.84 crore versus ₹0.5622 crore; related teaching/professional payments are separately disclosed, including Hiral Kapasi ₹0.21 crore, Sejal Shah ₹0.09 crore and Kirti Pangam ₹0.12 crore in the RPT note. Such payments require economic benchmarking, not automatic abuse assumptions. Branch setup capitalization is a KAM: commissioning dates, eligible salaries/rent and later depreciation determine when costs hit earnings. Two jointly controlled arrangements remained pre-operative with expenses capitalized. ZEAL associate profit ₹0.068 crore is small relative to its ₹4.4633 crore carrying investment, a roughly 1.5% accounting yield diagnostic, not acquisition IRR. [S1] The FY25 report fixes original ZEAL pricing at ₹8.67 crore for 51%, with ₹4.335 crore already invested. The revised timetable replaced the earlier October 2025 completion expectation with April 2026 control and performance-linked payments through FY29. September shareholders approved the dividend and bonus; October 17 opening demonstrates delivery of a branch, not proof of financial breakeven. The July 16 issuer letter expressly denies a Mahesh Tutorials acquisition and describes limited student coaching support; no takeover or assumption of its liabilities is included in the model. [S2 note 27, S5, S9–S11] Promoter ownership declined from 73.00% in FY23 to approximately 64.74% in March 2026. The March shareholding filing declares no pledged or otherwise encumbered promoter shares, warrants, convertibles or outstanding ESOPs; this is dated evidence, not blanket October clearance. [S12, S13, S17]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text: Three-year FY24–26 CFO totals ₹24.4773 crore versus reported PAT ₹15.0988 crore, or 1.621 times. Asset purchases total ₹27.1064 crore, leaving negative ₹2.6291 crore before separate associate investment and other financing payments. FY26 fee advances rose ₹3.5303 crore while receivables rose from ₹0.7703 crore to ₹7.2283 crore; contractual billing therefore consumes cash despite advance tuition. Signed May results and note totals support the receivable and operating-cash baseline where annual display lines differ. A historical FY23 comparative also omits the negative sign on ₹2.96 lakh CFO: the subtotal and net-cash bridge establish the analytical correction, retained beside the original presentation. These are reporting-quality caveats, not a claim of fraud. Opening tax, current employee provisions, long-term employee claims and the declared dividend are separately mapped in valuation. [S1, S6, S12, S13]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At ₹230 on October 7, market value is ₹278.5392 crore and reported FY26 owner-earnings P/E is about 30.6 times. The annual model uses core revenue, operating margin, working-capital stocks, maintenance and expansion capex, cash tax, opening claims, conditional debt and fallback dilution, then adds only 51% of ZEAL equity value. Bear/base/bull returns are approximately −19.3%/7.9%/27.8%. The central case uses 15% core growth, 17% EBIT and a normalized 16-times exit EV/EBIT; it needs no new debt or equity. About 23.2% growth is required to meet the 15% hurdle on otherwise unchanged assumptions. A 12-times exit lowers central return to about 2.8%. The full two-way grid, hurdle sensitivities and conditional entry prices are shown below; none is an observable fair value. [S1, S2, S4–S9, M1]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest failure path is weaker enrollment and fee-advance runoff while rent/faculty costs persist, followed by lower margins, acquisition cash demands and expensive financing. The ordinary bear loses roughly two-thirds of the dated entry value. With no new credit, that bear needs about ₹9.70 crore fallback equity before liquidating nonoperating investments; the severe linked stress needs ₹24.94 crore. Rescue is not guaranteed, and failure would mean curtailed expansion, asset realization or distress. A full-contribution removal of ₹7.483 crore other operating revenue is an explicit extreme recurrence stress, not an assertion that it is fictitious or nonrecurring. Positive CFO, no March bank debt and investment holdings are the strongest contrary evidence. [S1, S6, E7]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At unchanged multiples, 5×/10× in five years require 37.97%/58.49% annual per-share earnings growth. Revenue CAGR 44.64% is not enough by itself because it includes acquisitions and requires reinvestment; future ZEAL consolidation also changes reported scale without equivalent owner profit. Scenario returns use the post-bonus share count, explicit reinvestment and no unsupported probability of success.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Monitor the seven company-specific items below: core admissions/fees, contractual collections, tuition-advance obligations, ZEAL cash consideration, branch capitalization/commissioning, the exchange clarification and actual execution liquidity. Review at each material filing or results release. The zero-median trading baseline is not replaced by occasional high-turnover days; new bid/ask evidence is necessary before any implementation assessment. These are research checkpoints, not automatically scheduled reminders. [S1, S5, S8, S10, S16, M1]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: BQS and GQS describe mixed but source-supported business and growth quality; the price-dependent IAS falls in weak setup/value-trap risk under the v3.0 matrix. The decisive reasons are below-hurdle central return, meaningful impairment sensitivity and L 1 liquidity, not a blanket claim that every weakness is overvaluation. Research watchlist only: evidence of persistent same-centre returns and contractual collections could improve the business assessment, while a different verified price changes IAS independently. No holding size, transaction or personal suitability is inferred. [E1–E8]

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The review uses audited FY22–26 statements with FY21 comparisons, signed current results, acquisition terms, dividend/bonus notices, branch updates and dated official market data. Original ZEAL pricing is available; the revised earnout formula is not. Current parent-quarter growth and explicit SOTP avoid presenting acquisition consolidation as organic progress. Key uncertainties are contractual revenue collection, unit economics, government-balance composition, the incomplete exchange clarification entry and executable liquidity. Model assumptions are labeled and sensitivity-tested; public statements establish what was disclosed, not the truth of every forecast. [S1–S16, M1]

assumptions: Units are INR crore and crore shares. Five full operating years approximate a five-year holding period from the October 7, 2026 observed ₹230 close. March 2026 actual balances are bridged for the declared September dividend; no unreported quarterly cash or October balance sheet is invented.

Opening cash is 5.0452, including bank deposits classified by the issuer as cash equivalents. The declared pre-bonus dividend consumes 1.21104; it belongs to September 11 holders, not the October entrant. Gross opening income-tax provision 0.69 is paid in year one in addition to forecast current tax. No new IPO proceeds are credited.

Opening operating WC is 7.2283 receivables +0.8417 short advances +0.5827 prepaid expenses +0.8470 current security deposits −0.4793 trade payables −21.6385 other operating liabilities −0.3977 current employee provisions = −13.0158. Government balances 3.1337 and interest receivable 0.1218 are excluded as nonoperating claims; no recovery assumed centrally. Government-balance tax/GST composition is not separately disclosed, so full tax payment without offset is conservative and explicitly tested.

Long-term employee obligation 0.6223 is deducted at terminal. Current employee claims are already in WC and are not deducted again. Rent and teaching costs remain in EBIT; operating leases are not additionally capitalized as debt, avoiding a mixed lease convention. Future deposits, fit-out and setup are covered by the incremental capital allowance, not a claim about disclosed unit capex.

Base core sales growth is 15%, anchored to current comparable parent-quarter growth of 14.97% and continued branch launches, rather than 27.56% acquisition-inflated group growth. Seventeen percent EBIT is close to FY26 17.33% and parent TTM approximately 17.26%; a weak seasonal June quarter is not annualized. The 16-times terminal EV/EBIT normalizes the much higher dated entry multiple. These are analyst assumptions, not guidance.

An illustrative unit bridge combines 12% annual enrollment growth and 2.68% fee/mix growth. A 15,000-student index becomes approximately 26,435 after five years; the issuer reports more than 15,000, not an exact audited cohort. This is a required scale path, not verified seats or guaranteed admissions. No automatic earnings credit is given to an announced branch.

Growth investment is the greater of the 70%/30% completion allowance and incremental revenue divided by assumed fixed-capital turnover. The 3.3746 allowance equals historical CWIP but is an estimate of additional setup spending, not a disclosed remaining budget or re-spending of recorded CWIP. Maintenance capex equals modeled depreciation as an assumption; overrun and additional 0.9013 commitment stresses are shown.

Original ZEAL consideration was 8.67 for 51%, with 4.335 paid for the initial 25.5% in FY25. Revised May 2026 terms change remaining payment to performance-linked tranches through FY29 without a disclosed formula. Base remaining payment 5 is close to the original remaining 4.335 anchor, with bear/bull 10 and 0–15 sensitivities. It is charged in three annual cash tranches, not ignored or assumed to be a known liability.

ZEAL is valued separately at 51% of forecast PAT using FY26 total PAT 0.2667595, explicitly excluding 49% minority. No interim upstream distribution is invented. The prior associate carrying investment 4.4633 is not added again. June-quarter group accounts confirm consolidation but do not supply a quarterly balance sheet or cash flow.

Nonoperating bonds 3.35 and long-term fixed deposits 2.0438 are included at unchanged nominal book value at terminal, without invented investment returns. A zero-recovery sensitivity is provided; no independent executable market quote is claimed. These assets are not also credited as new opening cash.

Tax is 25.17% of positive forecast PBT with no loss-tax cash benefit. Conditional revolving credit is capped at 30% of revenue; fallback equity is priced at half the dated quote if the cash floor of 5% of sales cannot otherwise be met. Neither borrowing nor rescue issuance is committed. The no-new-credit bear and severe cases test funding dependence.

Terminal core EV equals EBIT times the assumed exit multiple, less debt and the long-term employee claim, plus only surplus cash and separately identified investments. ZEAL attributable value is added once, then divided by modeled diluted shares. No future dividends are assumed. Scenario probabilities are optional and are not required for a conditional R score.

GOV.reason: RPT pay and acquisition funding disclosed, but related service benchmarking and capitalization judgment remain; contrary: signed coherent statements and actual allotment terms verified.

MOAT.reason: Local network of 40 centres and teaching franchise support positioning; contrary: no proven faculty retention or same-centre pricing power.

REV.reason: Preselected three-year post-IPO window FY23–FY26 reported revenue 23.1181→63.4314 crore yields approximately 40.0% CAGR, starting score 9; acquisition mix and Medium-confidence organic decomposition limit the score to 8. Five-year FY21–FY26 is also shown but starts in the pandemic period. Contrary: current parent-quarter growth 14.97% is slower; one quarter alone does not change the historical rubric.

DUR.reason: New locations and additional ZEAL control expand addressable cohorts; contrary: maturation economics and earn-out obligations unquantified.

CAP.reason: Goodwill/CWIP-inclusive endpoint return proxy exceeds assumed capital cost; contrary: short acquisition history, capitalized setup costs and associate funding prevent high-conviction cohort returns.

CASH.reason: Three-year CFO 24.4773 / PAT 15.0988 = 1.621 times, and positive recent receipts support conversion. Contrary: advance tuition funds part of cash generation; receivables rose sharply and asset spending 27.1064 exceeds CFO. Historical FY23 conversion was weak and regrouped, so this is not cycle-proven exceptional cash quality.

BAL.reason: No March financial debt and positive base cash generation; reported cash and separately identified bonds/FDs provide buffers. Contrary: deferred consideration and obligations to teach remain real claims, and the no-new-credit bear needs9.70 crore fallback equity before asset liquidations. Base needs neither new debt nor equity; this does not guarantee severe-stress funding.

EXEC.reason: Expanded network and revenue growth demonstrate delivery; contrary: acquired growth and pre-operative arrangements not equivalent to mature-centre success.

EARN.reason: FY26 core operating EBIT grew materially, and parent TTM margin remains approximately 17.3%; associate profit is a small part of annual PAT. Contrary:7.483 crore other operating revenue is not separately decomposed, capitalization affects timing, and latest parent PAT grew 4.71% despite 14.97% sales growth. Full-contribution recurrence stress is provided, not an assertion that revenue is one-off.

R.reason: Base IRR 7.86% is 7.14 percentage points below the 15% hurdle, mapping to 2. Earnout 0–15 and tax-offset sensitivity do not change the broad below-hurdle conclusion; no probability calibration is required.

D.reason: Bear terminal value implies approximately66% price loss and new borrowing; without new credit, fallback equity9.70 crore is modeled. Base is self-funded, but severe fee runoff plus margin compression requires24.94 crore equity before investment liquidation, so recovery is not assured.

P.reason: At17% EBIT and16-times exit, approximately23.2% core revenue growth is needed to reach15% return, versus supported base 15%. Cutting exit to 12 times lowers base return to about2.8%; several favorable operating assumptions must persist.

L.reason: Only27/60 and 6/20 observed sessions, zero median turnover and eight sessions without an observed trade after October 7. Occasional turnover supports episodic tradeability, but no finite median-based exit and ₹184,000 lot granularity justify the bottom band. A stale close is not an executable bid.

confidence.qualification: Forecast uncertainty is substantial. Accounting display issues are reconciled where used; current execution is not verified.

gates.reason: RPT professional payments and related-business acquisitions are disclosed; no substantiated severe diversion or minority abuse identified in reviewed primary records. Benchmarking and acquisition performance remain constraints, not generic reassurance.

Signed results, note totals and cash reconciliations support a usable baseline despite annual display errors and historical regroupings. September 8 exchange query detail and any response were not retrieved; the incomplete entry is not a proven material misstatement. Contractual revenue and capitalization require monitoring.

Base case funds opening tax/dividend, earnout and reinvestment without new borrowing or equity. Fee runoff and margin compression create financing needs; rescue is modeled, not assumed committed. No demonstrated present default or unfinanceable essential obligation is established.

SM remains eligible, with episodic trading but a zero 60-session median and no observed trade after October 7. L 1, no finite conservative exit estimate and no executable bid/depth verification. This is not described as suspended or proven wholly untradeable; any implementation requires fresh lot-aware order-book evidence.

Verify an executable lot-aware bid/ask and current trading restrictions before any implementation conclusion.
